authoring.protocol: crates/fathom-analyze/calibration/g3/README.md §2 (what each act means) and §3 (how blame is assigned)
authoring.meaning: One row per flagged episode: what the reviewer would have done with the flag, and what they read to decide it. `accepted` means the flag earned the read — the episode was worth stopping for, whatever the findings said. `dismissed` names a code from the closed vocabulary `e4.6` ships, and `blame` names which part of the flag was the false alarm: `score` when the ranking raised a flag no finding justified, a detector id when that detector's claim is what did not hold. A dismissal with no `blame` charges every detector that spoke on the episode, which is ADR-001 §5.4's own rule — an unwanted flag charges whatever raised it.

labels.note: A new 189-line Dependabot triage script and a new scheduled workflow: the flag's claim is that an operator has to act on a workflow change, and a new scheduled job under `permissions:` is exactly that. The two `# shellcheck disable=SC2016` lines `lint_escape` named are inside the script that had to be read anyway, so the finding cost nothing extra.

dependabot[bot]'s semver-patch bump of `go-gh`: six lines across go.mod and go.sum. The flag came from the workflow axis, lit by the episode's other member — a regenerated agentic workflow lockfile, not a hand edit. Reading it could not have paid for itself.
labels.evidence: `git show 38c8ba5c51`: go.mod/go.sum, 3 insertions 3 deletions, trailer `update-type: version-update:semver-patch`, author `dependabot[bot]`.

labels.note: A minor bump of `google.golang.org/grpc` — 28 lines, all of them go.sum hashes and go.mod. The flag is the same lockfile-and-workflow axis; there is no decision in the diff for a reviewer to make.

`generated_edit` charged three generated files as hand-edited. The commit says they were regenerated — "upgrade gh-aw from v0.87.5 to v0.89.21 and recompile lock files" — so the claim does not describe the change: the detector can tell a generated file from a hand-written one, but not a regeneration from a hand edit. The change that did need reading (the `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` fix) is not what was flagged.
labels.evidence: `git show efe3c7630d` commit body; the three paths (`.github/workflows/agentics-maintenance.yml`, `dependabot-triage.lock.yml`, `issue-triage.lock.yml`) each carry `# This file was automatically generated by gh-aw`.
